videofix.scenes_title: A copy for the place it is going.
scenes: Your video looks right in Photos, but a recipient sees flat or unusual color. Check whether the source is HDR or Log and whether the destination expects SDR. Create a standard-color copy when that is the requirement, then check the received version. Keep the original for a future HDR edit.

Ask for the required codec, resolution and frame rate before converting. If H.264 MP4 is requested, an HEVC source can need a compatibility copy even when its color is already SDR. Export a short sample first and confirm it works in the actual editing project.

Select a batch when several videos need the same output goal. Mixed footage can still contain different colors, frame rates and dimensions. Check each result instead of assuming one successful clip proves the entire batch. Allow storage for the originals and the new copies.

Source information, export choices and a preview of the finished file help you make that separate copy with a clear purpose.

audio-compressor.scenes_title: Make the recording easier to use.
scenes: Save a copy of your recording to Files, then import it into the tool for the job. Trim empty material if you do not need it and choose a format the recipient accepts. Play the final file before sending it; a smaller attachment is only useful if the speech is still clear.

A long session can be easier to listen to in separate files. Use Auto Split to divide the recording, review the lengths and listen near the boundaries. This divides audio into parts; it does not transcribe the lecture or automatically name its topics.
An M4A file for an MP3 destination

Keep the original recording and make an MP3 copy for the app or person that requests it. Choose the quality with the recording in mind, then compare the output. A higher export bitrate does not restore detail that was already missing in the source.

audio-compressor.studio_body: Audio Compressor is made by Space Sheep Studio for the work that comes after recording. Keep the useful section of an interview, divide a long lecture into parts, or prepare a smaller file to send. The tools bring these everyday jobs together so you can move from a recording in Files to a clip you can use.

collage-maker.scenes_title: Different pictures. Different ways to share.
scenes: Start with the photographs that belong together rather than every photograph from the trip. Give a favorite image more room, then use the others to add context. Move and zoom the photos so faces, landmarks and edges fit the chosen layout before saving the final image.

Use a side-by-side arrangement when the relationship between two images matters. Put the subjects in a consistent order and frame them at a useful scale. Check the final image on the screen where you will share it so the comparison remains easy to read.

A long image can keep selected screenshots together as one file. Arrange them in reading order, check repeated headers and inspect the joins. The composition tool does not promise automatic overlap removal. For small text, use fewer screenshots if the finished image becomes hard to read.

sober-wins.scenes_title: A routine that leaves room for real life.
scenes: Open the app and choose No alcohol or Had a drink for today. The useful part is the honest record, not an answer chosen to protect a number. Check reward progress if you want to, then carry on with your day. The collection is optional alongside the daily tracker.

Virtual finds add a visual part to the routine. Review Collection and arrange your mini fridge when you want to make it your own. These are illustrated beer items, so look at the screenshots and consider whether that theme suits you. They are not physical rewards or a measure of recovery.

A drinking day, a missed entry and an incorrect entry are different things. Review what is actually recorded in History and use the available correction controls when needed. Earlier entries still matter beyond the current alcohol-free period. A pause can sit alongside that routine without replacing your record.
sober-wins.choice_title: Is Sober Wins your kind of tracker?

choices: A daily log with a visual collection

Use the daily choices and History without making the cabinet your focus.
The camera mirror and Apple HealthKit connection are optional.
Sober Wins is a tracking app. Its Panic button opens activities and does not call emergency services.
sober-wins.studio_title: A daily record with something of your own.
sober-wins.studio_body: Sober Wins is made by Space Sheep Studio around a small daily routine: record what happened, discover a virtual find and give it a place in the mini fridge. The log keeps the days in context; the collection gives you something visual to make your own. Use the parts that fit your routine, whether that is a quick entry, a look back through History or a short pause.
